> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2a261216dd80ceb97d5e96cfd4913d9bd50c7fdc` — the merge of head `20b9a7e83d58628f54244e9cafdd02c1d4abb9be` into base `69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2a261216dd80ceb97d5e96cfd4913d9bd50c7fdc && git checkout 2a261216dd80ceb97d5e96cfd4913d9bd50c7fdc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4 20b9a7e83d58628f54244e9cafdd02c1d4abb9be && git checkout -B drift-repro 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4 && git merge --no-ff 20b9a7e83d58628f54244e9cafdd02c1d4abb9be

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fe11d4dadf076eb6fc350ef02ba85a4e3309ccdd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-binder-package-scope.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/function-package-scope.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-function-package-scope.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-request-family.dogfood.test.ts + read in the tree at this head, not reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts (`resolvePackageScopedHolders`, `PackageScopedNameRefusedError`), packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts (`registerFunction`, `functionHoldersOf`, `unregisterFunctionsByPackage`), packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts (`handlerOwnerPackageId`), service-automation `engine.ts` `flowCallerPackage` / `armedFlowPackage` / `connectorNameRefusal`, `guard-refusal.ts`, `inner-refusal.ts`, `dag-traversal.ts` (node failure path), `run-resume.ts` (`resolveRunContext`), `builtin/connector-nodes.ts`, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (`isPackageScopedRefusal`), packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts and app-plugin.ts (the owner `app:ID`), docs/adr/0150 D3, D4, D5. `.changeset/32073-script-node-function-by-package.md` is prose, read for ②.

Inputs: card #32073 body and all five comments (triage 6760697254, claim 6767942931, step 0 6768303953, rulings amendment 6768322803, os-dev-report 6770696523); PR #32257 body, 12-file list and net diff against merge-base `dee2e920`; the check-runs on this head. Check-runs at review time: 23 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 11 in progress: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates. Green among the completed: Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Test UI. This record does not stand in for the 11 pending verdicts. The PR is a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Script node caller = the armed flow's package; an environment flow or override reads with no caller. RIGHT.** `AutomationEngine#resolveFunction(name, context)` passes `this.flowCallerPackage(context)`, unedited, which answers `armedFlowPackage(context.flowName) ?? null`. `armedFlowPackage` answers the loader's package only when the armed registration's source is `package`, so a `.custom` override, a runtime body and an unknown name are `null`. That is ADR-0150 D3's overlay paragraph ("never resolves from the package the overlay customizes") and D4's function row ("resolved in the package of the flow ... that names it"). `resolveRunContext` stamps `flowName: flow.name` on every run, so a subflow child's script node resolves from the child.
2. **Two-holder no-caller read becomes a refusal naming both. RIGHT.** `resolveEnvironmentWide` answers `ambiguous-in-environment` with every package holder. `functionResolverOf` throws `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`code` RESOURCE_CONFLICT, `status` and `httpStatus` 409). Never first or last match.
3. **D3 (c) refused. RIGHT**, and declared (changeset item 3). Step 3 of the core rule; the override reaches a holder outside P's closure only as a caller with no package, as the ADR says.
4. **Owner-less function is the platform holder. RIGHT** against the R2 ruling in D4: own function first, then platform alone answers; platform beside a reachable package refuses `ambiguous-in-closure`; platform beside any package refuses `ambiguous-in-environment` for a caller with no package. `functionHoldersOf` returns `environmentItem: () => undefined`, so no owner-less function is ever read as an environment item.
5. **Hook binder serves its own function. RIGHT, a widening.** `ownPackageFunction` reads `functionHoldersOf(name).packageItem(handlerOwnerPackageId(packageId))` and keeps `entry.packageId !== packageId` as the gate. Own-package-only is what step-0 Q2 (A) asked for ("keeps its own-package-only rule") and what the ruling adopted. The ruling's wording "resolves by D3 from the hook's own package" is wider than what is built (no closure step); the build takes nothing away, since a closure holder was refused on main too.
6. **`AutomationEngine#resolveFunction`. RIGHT**, declared as item 6. `FlowFunctionResolver` gains a second parameter; a one-parameter resolver is still assignable and still called. The only in-tree caller of either is the script node.
7. **A host objectql without `functionHoldersOf` is left unbridged. RIGHT (fail closed)**, declared as item 7. Falling back to the bare map would bring back the last-registration answer this card removes. The only in-tree provider of the `objectql` service is `ObjectQL` itself (objectql `plugin.ts:858`), which carries both `functionHoldersOf` and `registry`.
8. **Trigger door answers 400 FLOW_FAILED carrying `innerRefusal`, not 409. RIGHT.** D5's 409 is the answer of a by-name door for the name the address carries. Here the address names the flow, the flow resolved, the run was dispatched, and a node failed. The flow doors' declared answer for "ran and failed" is 400 FLOW_FAILED, and `details.innerRefusal` is the declared carriage for a refusal a node met (the same path a `create_record` meeting a 409 duplicate takes). A 409 at this door would say the flow's name is in conflict, which is the answer that door already gives for a two-holder flow name. The card's "409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT naming every candidate" is met at the read itself (`resolveFunction` throws status 409, pinned) and at the door as `innerRefusal.code`. This goes beyond the sibling `connector_action` refusal, which carries text only.
9. **Action target not wired. RIGHT per ruling Q1.** At this head the only readers of `resolveFunctionEntry`, `resolveFunction` or `functionHoldersOf` outside tests are the automation bridge and the hook binder. No action path reads the function registry.

### ② Semver level

- **Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/objectql`. Correct.** AGENTS.md rule 3: a non-protocol change, breaking or not, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no key, accepted value or metadata type changes. Siblings 31672 (subflow) and 31673 (action engine) declare the same pair.
- **Declaration lines:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset. The `!` is on the title and the changeset summary.
- **ADR-0087 marker:** one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with a true reason (no stored shape moves). Check Changeset is green.
- **The seven FROM→TO items, each against the tree:** 1 own over last registration (true; pinned in both orders). 2 no-package two-holder (true; pinned in unit and dogfood). 3 D3 (c) (true; pinned in both). 4 platform beside a package (true; pinned for no caller and through a closure). 5 two in closure (true; pinned). 6 `resolveFunction` throws (true; pinned with `code`, `status` 409, reason, candidates). 7 unbridged host (true; `packageScopedFunctionEngineOf` pinned). The widening paragraph is true and pinned. Each narrowing has a fix line.
- **No undeclared served→refused answer found at a door or at a published API used within its declared type.** I checked `AutomationEngine#resolveFunction`, `setFunctionResolver`, `FlowFunctionResolver`, the script node on every flow door, `bindHooksToEngine` / `ObjectQL#bindHooks`, and the objectql exports (unchanged bodies). Completeness gaps, none a served→refused inside a declared type:
  - **should-fix S1 — hook binder, engine shape.** `ownPackageFunction`'s guard moved from `resolveFunctionEntry` to `functionHoldersOf`. An engine carrying the first but not the second goes FROM its own function bound TO `undefined`, so the hook is refused 400 INVALID_REFERENCE. This is the same class the changeset declares for automation as item 7, and it is not declared here. Graded below must-fix because `bindHooksToEngine`'s parameter is the concrete `ObjectQL`, every instance of which has both members, so it is reachable only through a cast. Add one FROM→TO line beside the widening. If the seat reads a duck-typed engine as inside the contract, it is a must-fix.
  - **should-fix S2 — served by a different holder, not enumerated.** Item 1 covers only "one of them its own". Two more answers move without refusing: a packaged flow holding none, with one holder in its closure and another holder outside registered last, goes FROM the outside holder's function TO the closure holder's; and a packaged flow holding none, with the platform's function and a package holder outside its closure, goes FROM the last registration TO the platform's. The general paragraph implies both; the numbered list does not carry them. Add one line.
  - **nit N1 — doors.** The changeset names only `POST /automation/:name/trigger`. Every door that reports a failed run (a flow-type action, a screen-flow resume) carries the same FLOW_FAILED answer.
  - **nit N2 — an owner that is no installed package.** A function registered under an owner string that is not a package id is refused `outside-closure` for a packaged flow, and the fix line ("declare a dependency") cannot apply; the fix is an owner-less registration. First-party 0.
  - **nit N3 — a widening not stated.** After `unregisterFunctionsByPackage` of the last registrant, an earlier holder is now served where the bare map answered "no function". No source caller of that method exists.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions: []`.** Nothing to answer.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1 (text still saying an action target names a function).** Answered: deferring the phase-1 refusal sentence (`bare-name-one-holder.ts:400`) to the D9 backstop is acceptable. Two of the stale sentences sit in files this diff edits, see nit N4. The carrier "PR acceptance notes" disappears on merge; the seat records it on #31700, the card this one blocks.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2 and `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`.** **should-fix S3, to the seat:** the owed follow-up has no issue number ("noted, not filed"). After this lands, `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` teaches a script node as "a registered function" with no package rule, which is wrong for D3 (c). File the card before landing; 31741 is the sibling shape.
- **Serial constraint and #32239.** Nothing here depends on #32239. `resolveFunction` calls `flowCallerPackage(context)`, and that signature is the same on #32239. No semantic conflict: after it, the caller is read from the run's slot key, which is what this node should get. ⚠ #32239's head is now `f4b5e50a`, not the `4f64bc83` the dev's trial merge used. I read `flowCallerPackage` and `armedFlowPackage` at `f4b5e50a`; the merge itself is the seat's to redo at landing. `main` moved `dee2e920` to `ca2a2e91`; none of this PR's files changed in between.
- **Card line "Epic red-line review before landing".** A landing condition this record does not satisfy. The seat holds it.
- **`Fixes #32073` with the action half unbuilt.** Ruled (Q1 = A). The premise check holds at this head, see ① 9.
- **Ruling Q2 wording** ("resolves by D3" against own-package-only as built): recorded under ① 5; it narrows nothing. The epic seat, to whom Q2 was reported, may want the wording aligned.
- **Not judged further:** the function holder key is `app:ID` with `ID = manifest.id || manifest.name` (`app-plugin.ts`), and the caller is the loader's package id. If a manifest has no `id` and the two derive differently, a packaged flow's own function would read as `outside-closure`. This is the same key E2 relies on, and the dogfood file pins the equal case on a real boot.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real (ADR-0150 D3 steps 1 to 3 and D4's function row). It takes away no declared capability beyond what D3 (c) and the R2 ruling declare. Attempts to break it:

- **Two holders.** Each packaged flow runs its own in both registration orders; own beats a closure holder; no caller refuses naming both. Holds.
- **One holder, byte-identical to main.** The served value is the same wrapper and `effect` main built. Own, closure, environment-wide and platform CONTROLs are pinned; an unregistered name still answers "no function named" with no `innerRefusal`. The only one-holder answer that moves is D3 (c), declared. Holds.
- **Environment override with no caller.** `armedFlowPackage` is undefined, so the override reaches a holder outside P's closure and is refused when P and Q both hold the name, never served P's on its behalf. Pinned through `resolveFlowPrecedence`. Holds, per the ADR.
- **Platform beside a package.** See ① 4; pinned for both caller kinds. Holds.
- **Closure holder against an outside holder.** Pinned both ways. Holds.
- **Shape-matched refusal.** `isPackageScopedRefusal` is the same predicate as runtime `domains/meta.ts:1010`. The catch wraps only `resolveFunction`, so a refusal thrown inside the function's own handler stays a runtime failure. Any other throw propagates. Holds.
- **`code` and `status` per ADR-0112.** The thrown class is asserted with `code` RESOURCE_CONFLICT and `status` 409; the door is asserted as 400 FLOW_FAILED with `details.innerRefusal.code`; the hook refusals are asserted with INVALID_REFERENCE and 400.

Findings:

- **should-fix S4 — the node result's `code` is declared and not pinned** (`builtin/screen-nodes.ts`). The changeset states `code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'` readable as `$error.code`. No test asserts it; every assertion reads `innerRefusal.code`. Removing the `code:` line turns nothing red. Add one assertion on `$error.code` or on the failed step.
- **nit N4 — stale sentences in touched files.** objectql `engine.ts` `functionHoldersOf` docblock, inside the edited hunk, still says "a flow's or an action's function", against the new sentence in `package-scoped-resolver.ts` that an action target is no reader. `PackageScopedFunctionQuery`'s doc says the same. `hook-binder.ts` near line 207 still says a script node "resolves it with no package".
- **nit N5 — the guard comment in `screen-nodes.ts`.** "No `fault` edge routes a run past" is true. A `try_catch` container still catches a guard's throw (`dag-traversal.ts` checks `errorClass` only for the fault edge). That is the same property `connector_action` has and it lies outside the diff. The comment block above it ("only the metadata itself earns a guard") now sits oddly next to a guard on resolution.
- `function-package-scope.ts`, `flow-definitions.ts`, `plugin.ts`, service-automation `engine.ts`: the code agrees with the contract each docblock states. Resolution is at call time. No finding.
- `hook-binder.ts`: agrees with its docblock. A bind under `metadata-service` and an owner spelled without `app:` answer as on main. No finding beyond S1 and N4.
- The three test files assert what the PR claims. No finding beyond S4.
